title: Degradation explainability: deadline-aware progressive truncation profiles
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Problem: Under bursty traffic and partial multi-region outages we need predictable latencies while preserving useful output. Current options (hard rejects, coarse fidelity ladders) lack two things: (1) a graceful, deadline-aware truncation mode that steps down output while optimizing for semantic fidelity; and (2) explainability so callers can understand why output was degraded (important for customer support and automated fallbacks).
goal: Implement a deadline-aware progressive truncation profile and API-level 'degradation_reason' metadata. Profiles should be policy-configurable per-tenant and per-route and compose with the existing admission controller so SLOs drive truncation aggressiveness rather than binary accept/reject.
design_summary: We will implement a multi-stage truncation pipeline: 1) prefix/KV cache reuse and strict batching to minimize work; 2) length-aware token-budgeting that trims generation length proportional to remaining deadline; 3) content-aware summarization fallback (model-assisted or heuristic) when trimming would lose critical tokens; 4) optional early-return of partial streaming responses with a 'degradation_reason' code. Each stage attaches a reason code and estimated semantic-loss score. The admission controller will decide which profile to apply based on SLO burn rate, region health, and tenant priority.
comments: 2025-02-17 — Spike: implemented a prototype in sandbox runtime that applies token-budgeting based on request.deadline-ms. Measured single-region p95 latency improvement of ~42% for long outputs (>=400 tokens) when trimming by 30% on average.

2025-02-19 — Trade-off discussion in sync: PM wants explicit reason codes to be stable (enum) so client SDKs can map responses to retry/fallback UX. Design agreed on codes: NO_DEGRADATION, TRUNCATED_LENGTH, SUMMARIZED_FALLBACK, FALLBACK_MODEL, REJECTED_BY_ADMISSION.
2025-02-21 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123 (prototype truncation + telemetry). Requesting review from @maria-ops for observability hooks.

2025-02-25 — Load test: ran regional failover simulation (us-east degraded). With conservative profile applied to low-priority tenants, overall 99th latency remained below SLO for high-priority traffic; low-priority saw quality drop measured by embedding-similarity (mean similarity -0.06).
2025-02-27 — UX note from PM (R. Gomez): surface degradation_reason and estimated_quality_delta in the API so product teams can show 'trimmed for latency' banners or switch to async job behavior.
2025-03-02 — Security review: no new secrets access. Confirmed behavior respects KMS constraints. No further security blockers.
2025-03-03 — Engineering note: need to add regression tests for streaming partial responses and ensure client-side SDKs tolerate metadata changes (work item in SDK backlog).
acceptance_criteria: API returns degradation_reason enum in all degraded responses
Configurable truncation profiles per-tenant and per-route via admin API
Admission controller chooses profile based on SLO burn rate and region health metrics
Integration tests show p95 latency improvement for degraded traffic without violating high-priority SLOs in multi-region failover scenarios
Telemetry emitted: reason_code, estimated_quality_delta, tokens_saved, original_target_length
implementation_steps: Add token-budgeting middleware that computes 'allowed_tokens' from request.deadline and route profile
Implement summarization fallback hook (policy: prefer model-based summarize when token-cut > 40%, else heuristic sentence-trim)
Wire degradation_reason and quality estimates into response envelope and streaming path
Expose per-tenant profile configuration in control plane (admin API + console) with safe defaults
Teach admission controller to switch profiles based on SLO burn-rate thresholds and region health signals
Add e2e tests including synthetic spikes and a multi-region failover harness
Add dashboards and SLO alerts for degradation_reason counts and mean estimated_quality_delta
Rollout: start with canary for 5% of traffic, monitor similarity metrics and customer tickets, then increase to 100% if stable
risk_mitigation: Conservative rollout, strong observability (similarity-based quality metric + manual inspection), per-tenant opt-out flag. If summarization fallback creates unacceptable hallucination risk we will fallback to returning a short explicit 'TRUNCATED_LENGTH' with a pointer to async job. Telemetry will allow quick rollback and granular exclusion of affected tenants.
metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency by tenant and priority
mean embedding-similarity between original-output-snapshot and degraded-output (test harness)
SLO burn rate change pre/post rollout
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-budgeting math and enum conversions. Integration tests for streaming partial responses and metadata. Canary load tests: 1k rps spike with regional failover scenario. Run human evaluation on representative prompt set to verify acceptable semantic degradation (target: avg similarity >= 0.85 for trimmed outputs).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flags off in runtime; 2) Enable canary profile for non-paying sandbox tenants (5% traffic) + monitor 72h; 3) Enable for low-priority paid tenants (20%) and run 48h; 4) Expand to full population with per-tenant opt-outs; 5) Publish upgrade notes and SDK compatibility guide.
follow_ups: Create SDK mapping for degradation_reason -> client behavior (ticket in SDK backlog)
Add a self-serve console widget to visualize per-tenant truncation events
Explore ML model to predict semantic-loss and recommend truncation thresholds
